title: Anomander Rake, Son of Darkness
summary: Anomander Rake leads the Tiste Andii, the shadow-skinned people born of the goddess Mother Dark, and rules from Moon's Spawn, a mountain-sized fortress that floats and moves at his command. He carries Dragnipur, a black long-sword forged to imprison the souls of everyone it kills, binding them into an endless task none of them chose. Ancient even by the standards of his own long-lived kind, he has spent ages as a wanderer, general, and reluctant power broker, arriving in mortal conflicts only when the stakes force his hand. His first major appearance finds him and his Andii mercenaries drawn into the Malazan Empire's siege of a Genabackan city, where his intervention reshapes the balance of the war. Those who meet him find a being of terrible competence and quiet, world-weary sorrow, more concerned with old debts and older griefs than with the politics of the age.

title: Onos T'oolan
summary: Onos T'oolan is First Sword of the T'lan Imass, the undying warrior clans bound long ago by a ritual that traded flesh for endless vengeance against the Jaghut. He marches with Coltaine's refugee column across the Seven Cities uprising, choosing to shatter his own ancient bones defending the living rather than stand apart from them. A bond formed with a dying Malazan soldier's spirit later calls him back from destruction, and the return leaves him able to feel again after ten thousand years of numbness. He builds a new life among the White Face Barghast and takes a wife, but when that family is butchered he turns his grief into a war against the Ritual itself, gathering T'lan Imass who share his fury and marching to confront the very sorcery that made them deathless. His campaign becomes a reckoning over whether the undying clans owe the world an ending or another age of servitude.

title: Tellann
summary: Tellann is the elder warren claimed by the Imass, an aspect of magic tied to blood, bone, and the raw heat of living flesh reduced to its most stubborn essence. In the deep past, entire clans of Imass bonecasters channeled it in a single, world-altering rite that stripped their people of death and decay so they could pursue an unending war against the Jaghut, becoming the T'lan Imass. Warriors who draw on Tellann in its rawer form can push the body past ordinary limits, and its fire-edged nature makes it a poor match for otataral or ice-bound sorceries but a natural counter to enemies that rely on sheer numbers or slow undead resilience. Because the ritual that reshaped the Imass drew so heavily on this warren, Tellann is remembered by scholars less as a source of flashy spellcraft and more as the power of endurance, sacrifice, and a promise kept far longer than any single life.

title: Omtose Phellack
summary: Omtose Phellack is the elder warren claimed by the Jaghut, a realm of ice and profound stillness far older than the seven warrens later charted by human sorcery. Jaghut wielded it not for war so much as isolation, raising frozen wards and sealing themselves in glacial stasis to escape both their own kind and the ambitions of others. During the ancient Jaghut Wars the T'lan Imass built their entire existence around breaking Omtose Phellack's holds, shattering ice-bound seals and hunting down Tyrants who twisted the warren toward domination and undeath. Its power lingers in ruins, buried vaults, and the odd Jaghut relic long after most of its wielders are gone, capable of freezing flesh and will alike. Because it predates the mortal warrens, its cold cannot be shrugged off as ordinary winter magic, and even a fading echo of it can overpower an unprepared mage.

title: T'lan Imass
summary: The T'lan Imass are an undead warrior people descended from the First Humans, who gave up mortality entirely through the Ritual of Tellann so they could wage an unending war against the Jaghut. Their flesh has withered to bone and dried sinew, held together and animated by the ritual's binding rather than blood or breath, and they feel neither cold nor pain, though fire and the rare mineral otataral can still destroy them. Countless clans lie dormant across the world under the command of ancient First Swords and Bonecasters, rousing only when the presence of a surviving Jaghut is sensed. Individual T'lan Imass, most notably the solitary warrior Onos T'oolan, still carry fragments of the grief and loss they buried beneath the ritual, suggesting the vow that binds them is less absolute than the clans themselves believe.

title: The Warrens
summary: The warrens are hidden dimensions of raw power that sorcerers of the Malazan world tap into to work magic, each one carrying its own flavor, colour, and temperament rather than being a single generic 'mana pool.' Some are ancient and tied to entire peoples or ages — the Imass draw on one shaped by ice and endurance, the Tiste races each claim one bound to darkness, light, or shadow — while others are younger paths opened more recently and used more freely by human mages. Access is not universal: a mage is usually bonded to one or two warrens through blood, training, or luck, and forcing open a warrent that resists you is dangerous. Legend holds that the whole network of warrens exists because an ascendant bled himself into the void to make sorcery possible for those who followed, and that act still echoes in how warrens are described and warded. A few warrens are actively hostile to magic itself, capable of smothering other warrens nearby, which makes them prized as weapons as much as sources of power.

title: Soletaken & D'ivers
summary: Soletaken and D'ivers name the two branches of an old shapeshifting affliction rather than an ordinary bloodline: those touched by it can shed their given shape for that of an animal, and the split between the two names describes how the change happens. A Soletaken pours the whole of their will into a single beast-shape — often something formidable, on rare occasions a dragon — and remains one creature with one set of wounds and one mind to kill. A D'ivers instead fractures across many small bodies of the same kind, a swarm or pack sharing one intent, so cutting down any single body does almost nothing to the will driving the rest. The condition appears to reach back to the Elder Gods' age and can spread between the afflicted, part of why it is feared as much as any warren-born sorcery. Certain convergences are known to call to Soletaken and D'ivers with unusual force, drawing them toward gates of ascendant power almost against their own judgment. A handful of the afflicted are famous enough to be named individually rather than lumped in with their kind — a lord who wears a dragon's shape, a jackal-thing that has endured ages as a scattered pack, a tiger-souled warrior who climbed all the way to godhood.

title: The Path of Hands
summary: Among the Teblor of the Laederon Plateau, a young warrior earns true standing only by leading a raid beyond the mountains and returning with proof of blood spilled among the lowland tribes — this rite is known as the Path of Hands. Karsa Orlong sets out on his own Path alongside his companions Bairoth Gild and Delum Thord, driven by ambition to eclipse the legendary raids of his grandfather. Their crossing into settled lands ends in catastrophic reversal: ambush, capture, and years of slavery that strip away Karsa's certainty in Teblor superiority. What begins as a coming-of-age ritual becomes the hinge on which Karsa's entire arc turns, reshaping him from a proud tribal warrior into something the wider world will have to reckon with. The rite itself endures among the Teblor as tradition even as this particular Path becomes legend for how badly it went.

title: Otataral
summary: Otataral is a rust-red mineral found only in a handful of deposits across Seven Cities, most famously on Otataral Island, and it is the one substance known to smother sorcery outright. Anyone carrying enough of it becomes unreachable by warren magic and, just as importantly, is cut off from working any magic themselves, which makes it prized for shackles, blades, and armor meant to hold or wound beings that would otherwise shrug off ordinary weapons. The Malazan Empire treats the ore as a strategic resource, mining it with forced labor and arming key soldiers with otataral-edged weapons to police mages and even threaten ascendants. Prolonged handling of the raw dust is dangerous to the body, and at least one notable figure is maimed by exposure to it, left with a strange, unsettling second sight as a result. Because it strips away magical protection and regeneration alike, otataral is one of the few materials capable of truly killing beings who are otherwise nearly immortal.

title: Raraku
summary: Raraku is a vast desert in the heart of Seven Cities that was once the bed of an inland sea, its dried expanse now regarded as sacred ground by the desert tribes. It becomes the stronghold and spiritual heart of the Whirlwind uprising, sheltering the warcamp of the prophet Sha'ik and serving as the seat of the goddess the rebellion answers to. The wasteland is also bound up with older, stranger history: patches of fused glassy ground and stray deposits of otataral hint at cataclysmic violence wrought there long before the rebellion, tied to the wanderings of an ancient, dangerous being. Its isolation and hostility make it a natural fortress, drawing warriors, exiles, and pilgrims from across the subcontinent toward its center. By the time the rebellion reaches its climax, Raraku itself has become as much a character in the conflict as any army marching upon it.

title: Kruppe
summary: Kruppe is a rotund, endlessly talkative fixture of Darujhistan's streets who styles himself a dream-interpreter, minor merchant, and man of leisure, always speaking of himself in the third person. Beneath the comic bluster he is far sharper than he lets on, seeming to know things before they happen and steering conversations and events with an unsettling deftness. He keeps close company with the thief Crokus Younghand and the duelist Murillio, and proves instrumental in the tangled plots swirling around the city as outside powers move against it. Other characters consistently underestimate him, right up until his apparent foolishness is revealed as careful misdirection. His true nature and the full extent of his abilities remain deliberately obscured through the events of Gardens of the Moon.

title: Gryllen, the Tide of Madness
summary: Gryllen is a D'ivers — one sentient will spread across a vast swarm of rats that hunts, thinks, and hungers as a single creature. In Seven Cities his name is spoken with dread for the fall of Y'Ghatan, where the swarm poured through the burning streets and overwhelmed Malazan soldiers by the hundred, a memory that still marks the survivors. When the shapeshifters' convergence known as the Path of Hands draws Soletaken and D'ivers across the Holy Desert toward a promised gate of ascendancy, Gryllen moves with it, a tide too many bodies wide to fight with any single blade.
